newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Bally moves ahead on French restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Bally moves ahead on French restructuring.

text.p: Swiss shoemaker Bally Management AG said that the French authorities had given Bally-France approval to go ahead with a restructuring of the company.
"With respect to that, Bally can sell a portion of its outlets, or close them, and concentrate on 47 outlets in first-class locations," it said.

It said that a factory in Moulin and a distribution centre in Vierzon would be sold within the framework of a management buyout. Authorities gave Bally until September to find an alternative solution for another operation in Lyon-Villeurbanne, it said.
"For Bally-France, the acceptance of the restructuring plan allows for a new basis in which the concern once again has clear future perspectives," Bally said in a statement.
Bally said already in August that it planned the restructuring after the French operations recorded an operating loss. Bally-France employs around 1,200 people and has around 77 outlets.
Bally is owned by Swiss conglomerate Oerlikon-Buehrle.
